{{short description|Yemeni-Malaysian biochemist|bot=PearBOT 5}}
'''Eqbal Mohammed Abdu Dauqan''' (born 1980) is a Yemeni biochemist known for her studies of Biochemistry, nutrition, advocacy for refugees, and support of women scientists in her home country of Yemen and adopted country of Malaysia.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

She earned her bachelor's degree in biological chemistry in 2002 and a master's degree in [[organic chemistry]] in 2008, both from [[Taiz University]] in Yemen.  She earned her Ph.D. in biochemistry in 2012 at the [[National University of Malaysia]] under a scholarship from the [[Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World]], and remained there as a [[postdoctoral researcher]].<ref name=":0" /> In 2014, Dauqan received the [[Elsevier Foundation Award for Early Career Scientists in the Developing World]] for her work on antioxidants in vegetable oils.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.elsevier.com/connect/women-chemists-from-developing-countries-honored-for-research-of-natural-medicinal-compounds|title=Women chemists from developing countries honored for research of natural medicinal compounds|last1=Schemm|first1=Ylann|date=2014-02-18|work=Elsevier Connect|access-date=2017-06-21|last2=Bert|first2=Alison|language=en}}</ref>

She became a professor and Head of the Department of Medical Laboratories Sciences at [[Al Saeed University]] in [[Taiz]], Yemen.<ref name=":2" />  She earned acclaim for her popular writing.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />  In 2015, after her university was bombed and members of her family killed as part of the [[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)|Yemeni Civil War]], she returned to the National University of Malaysia as an assistant professor in chemical science and food technology, sponsored by the [[Institute of International Education]]'s [[Scholar Rescue Fund]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://twas.org/article/laboratory-far-home|title=A laboratory far from home|last=Serra|first=Cristina|date=2017-03-24|website=The World Academy of Sciences|language=en|access-date=2017-06-21}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.npr.org/sections/goatsandsoda/2017/06/20/530803655/she-may-be-the-most-unstoppable-scientist-in-the-world|title=She May Be The Most Unstoppable Scientist In The World|last=Doucleff|first=Michaeleen|date=2017-06-20|work=National Public Radio|access-date=2017-06-21|language=en}}</ref> She is now activity mentoring junior scholars who work in critical environments.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Dimitropoulos|first=Stav|date=2019-08-26|title=Biochemistry in a conflict zone|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-019-02565-w|journal=Nature|language=en|doi=10.1038/d41586-019-02565-w|pmid=32839592 |s2cid=203149549 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Dauqan was appointed as an associate professor at [[University of Agder]], Norway
through the Scholar at Risk Network, In September 2018, she had been selected as TWAS Young Affiliate for 2018-2022.
In May 2019 she was selected as a member of [[Global Young Academy]] (GYA) for 5 Years. In November 2019, she won the
UiA bridge cultural builder award for 2019 as a great ambassador for UiA. Currently, she is working in University of Oslo
(UiO), Norway through SAR as well.
